notes: This is a starter playbook covering frequent/important warning+error codes.
Prefer fixing issues over suppressing. Use -Wno-<CODE> or lint_off only when intentional and reviewed.
Some codes are version-dependent; update/extend based on your logs.

verilator:UNUSEDPARAM.cause: A parameter is declared but never referenced; often dead/legacy parameterization or unused config knob.
next_steps: If it’s truly unused, remove the parameter or use it (wire it into widths/logic).
If kept for interface compatibility (e.g., vendored IP), keep it and suppress only in that file/scope.
If the parameter should affect behavior, ensure it is referenced in the RTL (localparam/typedef widths, generate, etc.).
verilator:UNUSEDPARAM.suppress_with_waiver: Local lint_off UNUSEDPARAM around the declaration, or -Wno-UNUSEDPARAM for vendored code only.

verilator:UNUSEDSIGNAL.cause: A signal is declared but never used (or not driven and not used); can indicate missing connections or leftover scaffolding.
next_steps: If it should be connected, fix the wiring (especially TB interfaces like tl_i/tl_o).
If it’s intentionally unused, tie it off explicitly or remove it.
For testbench-only scaffolding, keep it but suppress locally if it adds noise.
verilator:UNUSEDSIGNAL.suppress_with_waiver: Local lint_off UNUSEDSIGNAL in TB scaffolding; avoid global suppression.

verilator:PINCONNECTEMPTY.cause: A named port connection is present but the reference is empty; usually a typo or incomplete instantiation.
next_steps: Fix the instantiation: connect the port to a real signal or remove the empty named connection.
If the port is intentionally unused, connect it to a dummy net and comment intent.
Re-run lint to confirm the instantiation is clean.
verilator:PINCONNECTEMPTY.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer fixing; suppress only if third-party IP and you cannot modify it.

verilator:TIMESCALEMOD.cause: Some modules/packages are missing `timescale while others have it; Verilator warns for consistency (IEEE 1800 timescale rules).
next_steps: Decide a project-wide policy: either put `timescale in all compilation units that need it, or remove it everywhere and set timescale via tool flags.
For vendored IP, avoid editing files: add timescale via wrapper/include or configure lint suppression for those paths.
Ensure TB and any delay constructs behave consistently after the change.
verilator:TIMESCALEMOD.suppress_with_waiver: Often safe to suppress in vendored IP; do not suppress if you rely on #delays in those files.

verilator:MODDUP.cause: A module/package is declared multiple times; commonly due to duplicate file inclusion, wrong filelist, or mixing generated+source.
next_steps: Check your filelist/build system for duplicated entries (same .sv compiled twice).
Ensure include guards / `ifndef around package headers if they are included textually.
If Verilator dedup is involved, ensure you’re not compiling multiple copies from different paths.
verilator:MODDUP.suppress_with_waiver: Do not suppress; MODDUP usually indicates a build/filelist problem.

verilator:DECLFILENAME.cause: Filename does not match the declared module/package name (or Verilator’s dedup-renamed name); often appears with dedup or packaging conventions.
next_steps: If this is your code: align file name and package/module name for clarity.
If this is vendored IP: consider suppressing to reduce noise.
If names include __Vdedup*, confirm you aren’t compiling duplicated packages/modules (see MODDUP).
verilator:DECLFILENAME.suppress_with_waiver: Safe to suppress in third-party packages once MODDUP is understood.

verilator:EOFNEWLINE.cause: Missing newline at end of file (POSIX style issue).
next_steps: Add a trailing newline at the end of the file.
If generated files trigger this, fix the generator or apply a formatting hook.
Re-run lint to reduce noise.
verilator:EOFNEWLINE.suppress_with_waiver: Safe to suppress, but it’s easy to fix automatically.

verilator:WIDTHEXPAND.cause: An argument/expression is narrower than expected and is being implicitly expanded; may hide truncation/extension mistakes.
next_steps: Make widths explicit: size constants to the expected width (e.g., use 8'h00 instead of 4'h0 when 8 bits are expected).
If the function expects a byte/word, cast or extend intentionally (zero-extend vs sign-extend).
Re-run lint and add a small directed TB check for the call site.
verilator:WIDTHEXPAND.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer explicit sizing; suppress only if the implicit expansion is intentional everywhere.

verilator:ALWCOMBORDER.cause: In always_comb, a variable is used before being assigned in that block (or assigned after use); can cause simulation mismatches or latch-like behavior.
next_steps: Add default assignments at the top of always_comb before any use (recommended pattern).
Refactor to compute into temporaries first, then assign outputs at the end.
Re-run lint; if needed add an assertion to catch X/uninitialized usage.
verilator:ALWCOMBORDER.suppress_with_waiver: Avoid suppression; usually indicates a real ordering/default assignment issue.

verilator:MULTITOP.cause: Multiple top-level modules found; Verilator can’t infer the intended top without --top-module or configuration.
next_steps: Set the intended top explicitly (e.g., --top-module <name>) in your build flow or Make target.
If using libraries, ensure non-top modules are not treated as tops (compile order / flags).
Re-run lint/sim with a single specified top.
verilator:MULTITOP.suppress_with_waiver: Do not suppress; fix by selecting the correct top module.

verilator:generic_warning.cause: Generic warning bucket (non %Warning-CODE or tool wrapper). The log often includes a URL that maps to a Verilator code.
next_steps: If the line contains https://verilator.org/warn/<CODE>, add that <CODE> to the playbook explicitly.
Otherwise, find the nearest %Warning-XXX line above for the real code.
Keep this bucket as a fallback only.

verilator:GENERIC_ERROR.cause: Generic Verilator error without a specific code (or the parser could not classify it).
next_steps: Scroll up to the first %Error line and read the exact message and file:line context.
Fix the reported construct (syntax/unsupported feature/parameter mismatch), then re-run lint.
If it mentions timing controls, add --timing or --no-timing to your Verilator invocation.

verilator:generic_warning.cause: Generic warning matched by a broad regex; could be from Verilator or a wrapper script.
next_steps: Locate the first warning in the log and identify whether it is Verilator (%Warning-XXX) or another tool.
If it is a Verilator code, add a specific playbook entry for that code.
If it is a known benign warning, consider a targeted waiver/suppression.

verilator:NEEDTIMINGOPT.cause: Your RTL uses timing controls (# delays, wait, event controls) but Verilator was not invoked with --timing or --no-timing.
next_steps: Decide the timing model: add --timing (simulate delays) or --no-timing (ignore delays) to the Verilator command.
If the timing controls are not needed for your flow, refactor the testbench to avoid delays and timing constructs.
Re-run the failing target and confirm the error disappears.

verilator:NOTIMING.cause: Verilator is running with a timing mode that conflicts with timing constructs present in the design/testbench.
next_steps: Check whether the build uses --no-timing and whether the testbench uses delays or event timing controls.
Switch to --timing if you need delay modeling; otherwise remove/guard timing constructs.
Re-run lint and simulation to confirm consistent behavior.

verilator:UNOPTFLAT.cause: Combinational loop or complex feedback prevents Verilator from flattening/optimizing the logic; often indicates a real design issue or a tool corner case.
next_steps: Inspect the reported signal path/instances in the warning and search for combinational feedback (assign/always_comb).
Break the loop with a register (clocked logic) or restructure the combinational logic to remove circular dependence.
Re-run lint to confirm the warning is gone; if it’s a known false-positive, isolate and suppress only that region.
verilator:UNOPTFLAT.suppress_with_waiver: Use a narrowly scoped suppression (lint_off UNOPTFLAT) only if reviewed/intentional; prefer fixing loops.

verilator:WIDTH.cause: Bit-width mismatch between LHS and RHS (assignment, operator result sizing, concatenation, etc.).
next_steps: Make widths explicit: size constants (e.g., 8'd3), cast or slice signals so RHS width matches LHS.
Check for unintended sign-extension/zero-extension; use signed/unsigned correctly.
Re-run lint to ensure the mismatch is resolved (avoid global suppression).
verilator:WIDTH.suppress_with_waiver: If intentional and reviewed, suppress locally or use -Wno-WIDTH as last resort.

verilator:UNUSED.cause: Declared signal/parameter is never used; can indicate dead code or missed connection.
next_steps: Confirm whether the signal/parameter should be used; connect it or remove it.
If kept for interface compatibility, document intent and suppress locally.
Re-run lint to confirm no unintended leftovers.
verilator:UNUSED.suppress_with_waiver: Local lint_off UNUSED or -Wno-UNUSED only when justified.

verilator:VARHIDDEN.cause: A variable declaration hides another variable from an outer scope; can confuse readers and cause subtle bugs.
next_steps: Rename the inner variable to avoid shadowing.
Consider refactoring scopes to improve clarity (e.g., separate blocks or functions).
Re-run lint to confirm the warning is resolved.
verilator:VARHIDDEN.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer renaming; if needed, local lint_off VARHIDDEN.

verilator:PINMISSING.cause: Module instance has missing port connection(s), often due to mismatched interface or forgotten wiring.
next_steps: Check the module definition vs instantiation; connect all required ports.
If a port is intentionally unused, tie it off explicitly and comment intent.
Re-run lint to confirm clean instantiation.
verilator:PINMISSING.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer fixing wiring; -Wno-PINMISSING only for known third-party code.

verilator:PINCONNECTEMPTY.cause: A named port connection is empty or malformed; can indicate a typo or incomplete instantiation.
next_steps: Fix the instantiation: connect the port to a real signal or remove the empty connection.
If intentionally unused, connect to an explicit dummy net/tie-off and comment it.
Re-run lint.
verilator:PINCONNECTEMPTY.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer fixing; -Wno-PINCONNECTEMPTY only if truly benign and reviewed.

verilator:PINNOCONNECT.cause: A port is not connected (or connection is missing) where Verilator expects one; similar to PINMISSING, often style/intent mismatch.
next_steps: Review the port map and connect missing ports or use explicit tie-offs.
Make intent explicit: if unused, connect to an unused signal with a clear name.
Re-run lint.
verilator:PINNOCONNECT.suppress_with_waiver: If unavoidable for third-party IP, use -Wno-PINNOCONNECT narrowly.

verilator:UNDRIVEN.cause: Signal is read but never driven (or effectively undriven); may lead to X/unknown behavior.
next_steps: Find all drivers: check reset/initialization and always blocks assigning the signal.
Ensure every path assigns the signal (including default assignments in combinational blocks).
Re-run lint and simulate with extra checks (X-prop if available in your flow).
verilator:UNDRIVEN.suppress_with_waiver: Avoid suppression unless you are intentionally modeling a floating/tri-stated net.

verilator:SYNCASYNCNET.cause: A net mixes synchronous and asynchronous control usage (e.g., used as both async reset and regular signal), which can be risky.
next_steps: Verify whether the net is truly an async control (reset/set) and keep it dedicated.
If it must be shared, consider separate signals: one for reset, one for functional logic.
Re-run lint.
verilator:SYNCASYNCNET.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer fixing; -Wno-SYNCASYNCNET only if reviewed and safe.

verilator:IMPLICIT.cause: Implicit wire/net declaration or implicit behavior that can hide typos and cause mismatches.
next_steps: Enable explicit declarations and fix typos: declare signals/ports explicitly.
Prefer SystemVerilog `logic` and explicit port directions/types.
Re-run lint with stricter settings in your flow.
verilator:IMPLICIT.suppress_with_waiver: Avoid suppression; implicit nets are a common source of bugs.

verilator:CASEINCOMPLETE.cause: Case statement is missing coverage for all possible values (may infer latches or unexpected behavior).
next_steps: Add a default case or complete all enumerated items (especially for full-width vectors).
If using enums, ensure all enum values are listed; consider unique/priority case semantics if appropriate.
Re-run lint and check whether LATCH warnings disappear.
verilator:CASEINCOMPLETE.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer completing the case; suppress only if formally proven safe.

verilator:CASEOVERLAP.cause: Case items overlap (multiple items can match); can produce ambiguous priority behavior.
next_steps: Fix overlapping patterns or switch to if/else chain with explicit priority.
If overlap is intentional, document it and use appropriate case style (unique/priority) carefully.
Re-run lint.

verilator:CASEX.cause: Use of casex treats X/Z bits as don't-cares and can hide real bugs; differs across tools/intent.
next_steps: Prefer case/inside or explicit masking comparisons rather than casex.
If casex is intentional, add comments and consider constraining X-propagation behavior.
Re-run lint.

verilator:CASEWITHX.cause: Case statement contains X values in items/expressions; can lead to tool-dependent behavior.
next_steps: Avoid X in case items; use explicit comparison logic or handle unknown states deliberately.
If modeling unknowns is required, consider assertions to catch illegal values early.
Re-run lint.
verilator:CASEWITHX.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer removing X usage; suppress locally only if required.

verilator:LATCH.cause: Combinational logic infers a latch (missing assignment on some paths).
next_steps: In always_comb, ensure every output gets a default assignment before conditionals.
Complete all branches (else/default) to avoid implied storage.
Re-run lint; also check for CASEINCOMPLETE contributing to latch inference.
verilator:LATCH.suppress_with_waiver: Avoid suppression; latches are usually unintended.

verilator:BLKSEQ.cause: Blocking assignments in sequential logic (always_ff/clocked always) may cause simulation-vs-synthesis mismatch and ordering issues.
next_steps: Use nonblocking assignments (<=) for clocked/sequential always blocks.
Keep blocking assignments for purely combinational always_comb only.
Re-run lint; watch for related COMBDLY/INITIALDLY issues in older code.
verilator:BLKSEQ.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer code fix; suppress locally only if the ordering is deliberate and reviewed.

verilator:COMBDLY.cause: Combinational delay (#) is present; Verilator timing mode may treat it differently and it can be non-synthesizable.
next_steps: Remove combinational delays from synthesizable RTL; move them to testbench if needed.
If delays are required for verification, ensure Verilator is run with --timing and confirm expected semantics.
Re-run simulation.

verilator:INITIALDLY.cause: Delay (#) appears in initial blocks; semantics may differ depending on timing mode and can be non-synthesizable.
next_steps: If synthesizable RTL: remove/guard initial delays and replace with reset sequencing in TB.
If TB-only: run with --timing and ensure delays are intentional.
Re-run simulation and confirm ordering.
verilator:INITIALDLY.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer refactoring; suppress only if the delay is intentional and verified.

verilator:UNSUPPORTED.cause: Design uses an unsupported SystemVerilog feature/construct. Verilator may ignore it or fail, possibly changing behavior vs other simulators.
next_steps: Read the exact unsupported construct in the error message and locate it in the code.
Replace it with a supported equivalent (often simpler synthesizable SV), or guard it with `ifdef VERILATOR` alternatives.
If you must keep it, consider blackboxing or adjusting the tool flow; confirm behavior matches expectations.
verilator:UNSUPPORTED.suppress_with_waiver: Suppressing UNSUPPORTED can hide real functional gaps; only do so with strong justification.

verilator:COVERIGN.cause: Coverage constructs are partially unsupported and were ignored; coverage results may differ from other simulators.
next_steps: Check which covergroup/coverpoint features were ignored and whether that matters for your verification goals.
If coverage is required, switch to supported constructs or a simulator that supports your coverage needs.
Do not assume coverage numbers are equivalent across simulators when this warning appears.
verilator:COVERIGN.suppress_with_waiver: If coverage is not required in this flow, you may suppress COVERIGN; document the limitation.

verilator:DECLFILENAME.cause: File naming/decl mismatch style warning; often occurs when module/class name and filename don’t align or include path issues.
next_steps: Ensure your file structure and includes match the project’s conventions.
If third-party code, consider leaving as-is and suppressing style warnings only.
Re-run lint to keep noise low.
verilator:DECLFILENAME.suppress_with_waiver: Consider -Wno-style to suppress style warnings as a group for third-party code only.

verilator:DEFPARAM.cause: Use of defparam is discouraged/legacy and can be fragile across tools.
next_steps: Replace defparam with parameter overrides in module instantiation (#(...)).
Confirm the overridden parameter values are what you expect after refactor.
Re-run lint.
verilator:DEFPARAM.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer refactor; suppress only for legacy third-party modules.

verilator:INCABSPATH.cause: Absolute include paths reduce portability and reproducibility.
next_steps: Switch to relative include paths or include directories provided by your build system.
Avoid hardcoding machine-specific paths in RTL/TB.
Re-run lint.
verilator:INCABSPATH.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer fixing; can be suppressed as style warning in third-party code.

verilator:ALWCOMBORDER.cause: Ordering/structure issue inside always_comb that may affect clarity or correctness (tool warns about style or implied behavior).
next_steps: Ensure always_comb blocks have clear default assignments and deterministic ordering.
Refactor complex always_comb into smaller blocks/functions for clarity.
Re-run lint.
verilator:ALWCOMBORDER.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer refactor; may be suppressed as lint/style in constrained contexts.

verilator:UNSIGNED.cause: Signed/unsigned mismatch can cause unintended arithmetic/compare results.
next_steps: Explicitly declare signedness of signals (logic signed/unsigned) and cast where needed.
Check arithmetic and comparisons for sign-extension or truncation.
Re-run lint and add directed tests for corner cases (negative values, overflow).
verilator:UNSIGNED.suppress_with_waiver: Prefer fixing signedness rather than suppressing.

verilator:MULTIDRIVEN.cause: A net appears to have multiple drivers, which can cause X/Z resolution issues or unintended behavior.
next_steps: Search for all assignments/drivers to the signal and ensure only one active driver exists.
If tri-state/bus behavior is intended, verify it is modeled in a Verilator-supported way (or refactor).
Re-run lint and simulate to verify the signal is stable.
verilator:MULTIDRIVEN.suppress_with_waiver: Avoid suppression; multiple drivers often indicate a design bug.

verilator:PORTSHORT.cause: Port connection shorted or ambiguously connected (e.g., same net to multiple inouts) leading to potential contention.
next_steps: Check the module instantiation and the directionality of ports.
Separate nets for separate port functions; avoid tying outputs together.
Re-run lint.
verilator:PORTSHORT.suppress_with_waiver: Do not suppress unless fully understood and safe.

verilator:lint_suppression.cause: You want to silence a warning for a reviewed, intentional pattern.
next_steps: Prefer local suppression around the smallest possible code region (lint_off/lint_on with the specific code).
Avoid global -Wno-<CODE> unless the entire codebase shares the same reviewed rationale.
Document why suppression is safe and add tests to guard behavior.
verilator:lint_suppression.suppress_with_waiver: Use -Wno-<CODE> or lint_off/lint_on only when justified; see Verilator docs and manpage.
